from: September book, night 7 (Praise with Every Breath)
p1: The very last psalm is a big, happy song. It says, “Praise Him with the sound of the trumpet. Praise Him with the harp.”
It says to praise Him with dancing and a jingly drum called a timbrel. Then come strings, pipes and loud, clashing cymbals!
The song asks everyone to praise the Lord with all they have.
p2: It ends, “Let every thing that has breath praise the Lord.” If you can breathe, you can praise Him! Once, children in the temple shouted “Hosanna” to praise Jesus. Jesus said their praise was perfect.
Take a big breath and let it out slowly. Every breath is a gift, and every breath can praise Him.
old: The very last songs in the Psalms are the happiest of all! They shout, “Praise Heavenly Father!” over and over with joy.
The song calls to everyone and everything: “Sun and moon, praise Him! Shining stars, praise Him! Mountains and trees, praise Him!”
Even the animals join in! “Whales in the sea, birds in the sky, little bugs and big lions — praise Heavenly Father!” All of creation says thank You to the One who made them.
And then the very last line: “Let EVERYTHING that breathes praise Heavenly Father!” That means you too — with singing, clapping, and a happy, thankful heart.
The whole world is like one big, joyful song to Heavenly Father. And you get to be part of it! Isn’t that wonderful?
